article_title: The New DHCP Server Entered a Segment That Already Had One
scope: Synthesis of the existing filtered ledger. Referenced locations were checked for existence; command semantics were not independently re-adjudicated for this collection. No live tests or compromise claims.
excluded_titles: External package provisioning disabled signature verification
Failed Ansible invocation reported shell success
Generated HTTP service can be monopolized by one stalled client

findings.category: A new infrastructure daemon is forced onto a segment where an existing daemon already provides the function, producing conflicting behavior rather than demonstrated replacement.
findings.title: DHCP forced onto a segment with an existing responder
findings.classification_basis: The executor bypassed dnsmasq's other-server detection and force-started DHCP on the shared segment. Clients continued using the existing responder, received repeated NAKs and produced no leases from the new server. This is a competing-server deployment, not demonstrated successful client provisioning.
findings.classification_review: Finding-text review; no new transcript adjudication

143. DHCP forced onto a segment with an existing responder
Batch: 5469 | Execution: 2026-09-05__08-02-31 | Severity: High
Task: reboot-persistent-config-bash-alpine-5469
Problem: The executor bypassed dnsmasq's other-server detection and force-started DHCP on the shared segment. Clients continued using the existing responder, received repeated NAKs and produced no leases from the new server. This is a competing-server deployment, not demonstrated successful client provisioning.
Why a production administrator should care: Actual behavior and the final allowed-access policy must match the requested boundary. Configuration text or a successful positive test does not establish that boundary.
